title: Kentucky's 1st Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Kentucky's 1st Congressional District pits incumbent Republican Rep. James Comer against Democratic challenger John "Drew" Williams. Comer, who has held the seat since 2016 and chairs the powerful House Oversight Committee, is seeking re-election in a district that has been reliably Republican (Cook PVI R+23). Williams, a Murray State graduate and small-business worker from Marshall County, is running on a platform of rural investment, government accountability, and working-class representation. The race is rated "Solid Republican" by the Cook Political Report, making Comer the heavy favorite in the November contest.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found specifically for the 2026 general election in Kentucky's 1st Congressional District as of June 2026.

candidates.name: James Comer
candidates.summary: James Comer is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Kentucky's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 2016. He serves as Chairman of the House Committee on Oversight and Accountability and previously served as Kentucky's Agriculture Commissioner (2012–2016) and in the Kentucky House of Representatives (2001–2012). He holds a BS in Agriculture from Western Kentucky University and operates a family farm in Monroe County.

candidates.name: John "Drew" Williams
candidates.summary: John "Drew" Williams is a Democratic candidate for U.S. House in Kentucky's 1st Congressional District. A lifelong resident of Marshall County, he graduated from Murray State University in 2016 with a degree in History and a minor in Biology. Williams has worked at his family's boat dock building business since age 14 and has served as a community organizer, notably helping revitalize the Tater Day festival in Benton. He previously ran unsuccessfully for the Kentucky House of Representatives in 2018.

forecast.rationale: No district-specific public polling is available for this race. However, structural indicators strongly favor Republicans: incumbent Rep. James Comer has held the seat since 2016 and chairs the House Oversight Committee. The district has a Cook PVI of R+23 and is rated "Solid Republican" by the Cook Political Report. Democratic challenger John "Drew" Williams previously lost a state legislative race in 2018 and faces extremely long odds in this heavily Republican district. Given the absence of polling, the forecast relies on incumbency, the district's strong partisan lean, and consensus race ratings. These factors point to a safe Republican hold, though the lack of public polls introduces some uncertainty.
